title: Does the diff reach a surface the app serves
description: One noul asked at /task Step 2.6's second skip condition, beside the glob match that decides it. The glob stays in charge; this answer is recorded and read by nothing.
actsNote: Nothing acts on an answer from this set. Nothing-acting is the safety mechanism, not shadow mode. See docs/adrs/0008-no-question-set-acts-in-this-campaign.md.
wiredInto: /task Step 2.6, second skip condition — registered as the step-2.6/surface site in src/toolkit/lib/judge-run.mjs
wiredIntoNote: Wired means asked and recorded, never consulted. The site carries acts: false like every other, so the wiring adds a row to the corpus and no branch to the run.

scope.statement: THE GLOB DECIDES AND KEEPS DECIDING. Step 2.6 skips when no changed file matches a routes glob and nothing else in the diff reaches a served surface. That check is unchanged, it runs first, and its answer is the one the run acts on. This set is asked at the same point and its answer goes into the report beside the glob's, which is the whole of what it does.
scope.note: A glob matches a path. Whether a changed file reaches something a user is served is a reachability question about the app, and the two disagree in both directions: a helper under a non-route path can be imported by every page, and a file sitting under a routes glob can be dead. Those disagreements are the only reason to ask at all.

loadShedding.statement: THIS SITE SHEDS WORK RATHER THAN ADDING IT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS PROMOTED LAST. A wrong high answer costs one wasted verification round. A wrong low answer silently skips the verification of a change that did reach a served surface, and nothing downstream notices — the run reports skipped, the PR opens, and the missing check leaves no trace. Jev may add work; Jev may never skip work.
loadShedding.consequence: Promotion of this set is therefore the last promotion in the campaign, behind a passed ADR 0013 bar and behind its own superseding ADR. Any promotion that did happen may only let a high answer ADD a verification round the glob would have skipped, never let a low answer withhold one the glob would have run.

carries: the changed-file list for this run
the routes globs the repo's run contract declares, and whether each changed file matched one
a bounded shape-only digest of what the diff changed in each file
state.note: Path-shaped and diff-shaped, not conversational. The question is about files and what serves them, so the digest needs no goal, no user prose and no transcript. Conversation-derived state leaving the device is gated twice, off by default, and printable with --dry-run.

eval.statement: THE LABEL IS THE VERIFIER'S OWN VERDICT, WHICH THE RUN COMPUTES MINUTES LATER AND ALREADY WRITES DOWN. Step 2.6 ends by recording its outcome with `my-command-tools shots record --tier <tier> --verdict <verdict> --rounds <n>`, whatever the verdict. A run that went on to exercise a surface — green or red — is a run where the diff reached one, which is the high label. A run that came back skipped or unverified for want of a surface is the low label. Nothing has to be re-derived, re-queried or paired against a separate store: the row and its label are produced by the same run, on the same branch, within minutes of each other.
eval.whyThisLabel: It is the cleanest and the highest-volume label available anywhere in this campaign. Clean, because the verdict is a value the run computes and writes rather than a state inferred from a transcript — which is exactly what ADR 0014 found missing when Subject B yielded 3 labels against a floor of 200. High-volume, because every /task run reaches Step 2.6 and records an outcome there, so the corpus grows with ordinary use rather than with a replay campaign nobody has authorised.
eval.cost: FREE. The run records the verdict whether or not --jev was ever passed, so collecting this label adds no gate, no call, no commit and no spend. The only new cost is the question itself, and that is bounded by the run's own token cap.

confound.statement: SKIPPED IS AMBIGUOUS UNLESS THE RUN SAYS WHICH SKIP FIRED. Step 2.6 has two skip conditions, and only the second is about surfaces — the first fires when the repo has no run contract and no dev/start/preview script, which says nothing about whether the diff reached a surface. A row labelled from a bare skipped is unusable.
confound.resolution: Step 2.6 already requires it: 'check both first, and record whichever fired'. A row whose recorded skip is condition 1, or whose skip reason was not recorded at all, is DROPPED from the corpus rather than scored — the same treatment ADR 0011 gives a pre-filtered comment, and for the same reason: scoring the cases the question was never about inflates the number.

eval.barNote: NO PRE-REGISTERED BAR COVERS THIS SET. ADR 0013 fixed bars for Subject A and Subject B only, and this is neither. A number collected here is a number and nothing more until a superseding ADR states the bar it would have to clear, and under ADR 0019 that bar is the last one in the campaign to be written.
eval.corpusNote: NO CORPUS EXISTS YET. Wiring the site records rows only from runs made with --jev on a device carrying a key, and the flag is off by default. Read this field again before quoting a number from it.

questions.noul: The diff reaches a surface the app serves: something a user is served is rendered differently, behaves differently, or returns different data because of these changes.
questions.clause: nothing else in the diff reaches a served surface
questions.answerMeans: 1.0 means the diff reaches a served surface, so Step 2.6 has something to exercise. 0.0 means it touches nothing the app serves, which is the condition under which the step skips.
questions.why: The glob answers a question about a path, and this is a question about reachability. A shared helper, a query, a schema or a config file can change every served page without matching any routes glob, and a file under a routes glob can be unreferenced — so the two answers come apart in both directions, and the second half of the skip condition is written in prose precisely because no glob expresses it.
